default_pending.why_not_yet: persuade-20 leaks two held-out lowercase-name spans that ASAP-AES never exercised in the same context, so its carrier recall is 84.2% against a 100% bar. Making it the default before that is fixed would put a red gate on main. The corpus, its plan and its measured baseline all ship now so the defect is visible and reproducible; the default flips in a follow-on change once the leak is closed.

resolution: VICARY_EVAL_CORPUS names a corpus id directly and wins outright.

Failing that, if an operator TSV is configured (VICARY_EVAL_CORPUS_TSV or _DIR) the corpus named by `operator_default` applies, so a machine that has always measured ASAP-AES keeps measuring ASAP-AES and does not silently change its answer.
Failing both, `default` applies. It is a shipped corpus, so the three corpus gates are measured on a fresh checkout with no operator setup at all.
why_this_file: Ports enumerate corpora from here rather than globbing the directory, so a half-added corpus — a profile written but not registered, or registered but not written — fails loudly on the next run instead of changing what a glob happens to return. The three corpus gates are keyed by these ids in carrier.json and measured.json; an id that appears in one and not the others is what those files' own checks are for.
